messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Japanese, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (locked meaning) | Target Requirement (Japanese morphosyntax) | |-------------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------| | Ahi | Exclamation of emotional intensity | Interjection **ああ**; literal back‑translation check: *“Ah!”* | | quanto | Marks degree of difficulty (“how”) | Degree adverb **どれほど** preceding the predicate; back‑translation: *“how”* | | a | Introduces infinitive purpose (“to”) | Particle **に** marking purpose after the verb stem; back‑translation: *“to”* | | dir | Action of speaking/telling | Verb **言う** in infinitive form **言うこと**; back‑translation: *“to tell”* | | qual | Refers to the unknown identity (“what”) | Interrogative pronoun **何** used as a nominal relative clause; back‑translation: *“what”* | | era | Past state of X (the forest) | Past copular **だった** attached to the noun phrase; back‑translation: *“was”* | | è | Present state of X as a “hard thing” | Present copular **だ** linking subject to predicate; back‑translation: *“is”* | | cosa | The entity being described (X) | Noun **もの** (generic “thing”); back‑translation: *“thing”* | | dura | Property indicating difficulty (“hard”) | Adjective **難しい** (hard/difficult) with degree marker **とても** for emphasis; back‑translation: *“hard”* | | esta | Demonstrative pointing to the specific forest (“this”) | Demonstrative adjective **この** modifying the noun; back‑translation: *“this”* | | selva | The referent X (forest/wood) | Noun **森** (forest) or **林**; back‑translation: *“forest/wood”* | | selvaggia | Property of X (“wild”) | Adjective **野生の**; back‑translation: *“wild”* | | e | Links adjectives (“and”) | Coordinating conjunction **そして** (or simple **、**) between adjectives; back‑translation: *“and”* | | aspra | Property of X (“rough”) | Adjective **荒い**; back‑translation: *“rough”* | | e | Links adjectives (“and”) | Same as above (**そして** or **、**); back‑translation: *“and”* | | forte | Property of X (“strong/dense”) | Adjective **濃い** (dense) or **強い** (strong) with degree marker **とても** if needed; back‑translation: *“strong/dense”* | | che | Relative pronoun referring back to *selva* (“which/that”) | Relative clause marker **～こと** or **～の** after the noun; back‑translation: *“which/that”* | | nel | Locates the mental activity (“in the”) | Prepositional phrase **…の中で**; back‑translation: *“in the”* | | pensier | Mental arena where X is considered (“thought”) | Noun **思考** or poetic **思ひ**; back‑translation: *“thought”* | | rinova | Causes the state of fear to re‑appear (“renews”) | Verb **新たにする** or **呼び起こす** in present tense **呼び起こす**; back‑translation: *“renews”* | | la | Definite article specifying “the fear” | Demonstrative **その** modifying the noun; back‑translation: *“the”* | | paura | Emotional response evoked by X (“fear”) | Noun **恐怖**; back‑translation: *“fear”* | | ! | Marks exclamation, heightening affect | Sentence‑final punctuation **！**; back‑translation: *“!”* |
**Notes on comparative ordering & degree** - The phrase “quanto … dura” is rendered with the explicit degree construction **どれほど…難しいか** (literally “how difficult it is”). - Adjectives “aspra” and “forte” are each preceded by **とても** when a stronger degree is required, preserving the intensity of the original Italian.
**Literal back‑translation check (full sentence)** > ああ、どれほど**言うこと**が**難しい**か、**この****森**は**野生の**、**荒い**、**とても濃い**ものだ、**それ**を**思考**の中で**呼び起こす****その恐怖**！
(Back‑translation: “Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell, this forest is wild, rough, and very dense, which in thought renews that fear!”)

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.
- Line 4: ああどれほど言うことが難しいか / それは難しいものだ / それはかつてそうだった - Line 5: この森は野生だ / 荒くて / 濃い - Line 6: それは / 思考の中で / 恐怖を呼び起こす

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Japanese lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura
**Line Inventory:** - ああどれほど言うことが難しいか - それは難しいものだ
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional content words were added. - The two phrases were concatenated directly; the ending copula 「だ」 of the second phrase provides the sentence‑final predicate.
**Target Text:** ああどれほど言うことが難しいかそれは難しいものだ
---
**Source Line:** 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte
**Line Inventory:** - この森は野生だ - 荒くて - 濃い
**Assembly Notes:** - Inserted the particle 「で」 after 「野生だ」 to link the adjectival clause smoothly (function word only). - The conjunctive 「荒くて」 already contains the connective 「て」, so no further particles are needed.
**Target Text:** この森は野生だで荒くて濃い
---
**Source Line:** 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura!
**Line Inventory:** - それは - 思考の中で - 恐怖を呼び起こす
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra words were required; the three phrases were placed in the natural order of a relative clause.
**Target Text:** それは思考の中で恐怖を呼び起こす！

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #: 4 Target Text: ああどれほど言うことが難しいかそれは難しいものだ Back-Translation: “Ah how hard it is to say, it is a hard thing.” Reference Translation: Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell … Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: (none)
- Line #: 5 Target Text: この森は野生だで荒くて濃い Back-Translation: “This forest is wild, rough and dense.” Reference Translation: … this wild and rough and dense wood … Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <FAIL> Meaning Drift <FAIL> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: この森は野生だが荒くて濃い
- Line #: 6 Target Text: それは思考の中で恐怖を呼び起こす！ Back-Translation: “It renews the fear in thought!” Reference Translation: … which in thought renews the fear! Checks: End Punct <OK> Coverage <OK> Meaning Drift <OK> Comparative Orientation <N/A> Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text: (none)
